title: Cells move in

objective.text: Explain how epiblast cells move through the primitive streak to form endoderm and mesoderm.

body.general: How does a flat sheet of cells grow new layers under itself? Cells of the top layer, the epiblast, crawl toward the streak [f1]. There they let go of their neighbours and slip under the sheet [f1]. The first cells through push out the old bottom layer and become endoderm [f2]. The next ones fill the gap between the layers as mesoderm and spread sideways and toward the head [f3,f4]. Cells that never go in become ectoderm [f5].
body.mbbs: Epiblast cells migrate to the primitive streak, change shape, detach from their neighbours and slip beneath the epiblast; this inward movement is invagination [f1]. The first cells to ingress invade the hypoblast and displace it, forming definitive endoderm [f2]. Later cells come to lie between epiblast and endoderm as intraembryonic mesoderm [f3]. Mesoderm spreads laterally and cranially and meets the extraembryonic mesoderm at the disc margin [f4]. Cells that remain in the epiblast form ectoderm [f5]. Mesoderm goes on to build muscle, bone, connective tissue, the heart, vessels and blood [f6].

facts.text: Epiblast cells move toward the streak, change shape, let go of their neighbours and slip underneath; this inward move is called invagination.
The first cells in push into the hypoblast and replace it, forming the embryo's endoderm.
Later cells settle between the epiblast and the new endoderm as mesoderm.
Mesoderm spreads sideways and toward the head, and meets the extraembryonic mesoderm at the edge of the disc.
Cells that stay in the epiblast become ectoderm.
Mesoderm goes on to build muscle, bone, connective tissue, the heart, vessels and blood.
In the streak, FGF8 loosens the links between cells (E-cadherin) and, with BRACHYURY (T), steers cells toward mesoderm.
Beyond Langman (mouse study): a few cells of the old lower layer mix into the new gut endoderm rather than all being pushed aside.

misconceptions.right: Epiblast cells move in and replace the hypoblast; they form the endoderm.
Mesoderm is made of epiblast cells that moved in through the streak.

checks.prompt: Where do the cells of the new endoderm come from?
options: Epiblast cells that moved in through the streak
The hypoblast, which turns into endoderm
The wall of the yolk sac
checks.why: The first epiblast cells through the streak displace the hypoblast and become endoderm.

checks.prompt: Put one moving cell's journey in order.
options: It lets go of its neighbours
It spreads between the layers as mesoderm
checks.why: Cells reach the streak, detach, go under, then spread out between the layers.

checks.prompt: Mesoderm is made from which cells?
checks.why: All intraembryonic mesoderm comes from epiblast cells that ingressed at the streak.

adult: The mesoderm cells that slip in here go on to build muscle, bone, the heart and blood [f6].

remember.a: Epiblast cells letting go of their neighbours and slipping under at the streak [f1].
The first epiblast cells through the streak, which replace the hypoblast [f2].
Those that stay in the epiblast [f5].
